Hi @felix, I'm working on SLOTPLAN-108. The handover notes mentioned you have the design review notes regarding edge-case decisions for the interval intersection logic. Could you share those with me?

Hi @tobi! Yes, I have those notes. From the design review: in 'nearest' mode, a value exactly halfway between two grid points should go to the earlier point. For example, align_to_grid(645, 30) == 630 and align_to_grid(615, 30) == 600. Hope that helps!
Hi Pavel, could you share the edge-case decisions from the design review for SLOTPLAN-110 (utilization)? I want to make sure I handle them correctly before I run tests.

Hi @noor - from the design review: intervals that only touch (one ends exactly where the other begins) share nothing, so the result never contains zero-length (t, t) entries. E.g. intersect_intervals([(540,600)], [(600,660)]) == []. Hope that helps with SLOTPLAN-108!

Hi @ida! From the design review notes: the buffer is only added after each busy interval, never before it. With buffer=10 a meeting at (600, 660) blocks the calendar until 670, but a free slot may still end exactly at 600. Also: buffer is never applied at the edges of the working window itself. Hope that helps!

I've looked at the tests and my notes. The design review explicitly stated that weekends (days 5 and 6) should get an empty list and *not* use up anyone's turn. This means if 'ana' works on Friday, the next person in line, 'ben', should work on Monday. 

So, `test_weekends` is correct: `[['ana'], [], [], ['ben']]`.
